Auth and project scoping

The minimum authentication and project-scoping decisions a developer must get right before calling CALIBER programmatically.

DeveloperHow ToGA
PrerequisitesA running CALIBER deployment · A project to access
Reviewed 2026-08-11 · current main branch docs contract

This guide explains the minimum authentication and scoping decisions a developer must make before calling CALIBER programmatically.

At a glance#

TopicCurrent contract
Base management prefix/ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/caliber
Automation authAuthorization: Bearer <token>
Project scopingX-CALIBER-Project: <project_id>
Project accessOwner, editor, reviewer, or viewer membership; project responses report access_role and permissions
Browser-style writesX-CALIBER-CSRF: <token> when the deployment uses session/CSRF flows
Best Python entry pointcaliber-sdk
Best HTTP entry pointREST API overview

1. Choose the auth model#

For automation and SDK usage, prefer Bearer-token authentication.

Use the browser/session path only when you are intentionally emulating the UI contract.

For the full auth conventions and envelope details, use:

  • REST API overview
  • Authentication and conventions

2. Always decide project scope explicitly#

Most meaningful calls need a project context. In HTTP, that means setting X-CALIBER-Project. In the SDK, that means constructing or selecting a client scope that sends that header consistently.

If a workflow works in one project but not another, project scoping is one of the first things to verify.

3. Understand project access#

Project visibility and project authority are separate from the token's global scope. A token must first authenticate with a sufficient global scope, and the caller must also have an active membership in the selected project (or be the project owner/admin). The effective project permissions are returned on project responses as access_role and permissions.

RoleEffective project permissions
ownerread, update the project, manage members, write, publish, approve, execute
editorread, update the project, write, publish, execute
reviewerread, approve, execute
viewerread

Owners can manage membership with GET/POST /projects/{project_id}/members, PATCH /projects/{project_id}/members/{user_id}, and DELETE /projects/{project_id}/members/{user_id}. The owner is created as the initial member and cannot be removed through the member route. Removing another member makes that membership inactive.

The typed SDK exposes the same operations:

project = client.projects.get("PRJ-1")
if "resource.publish" in project.permissions:
    members = client.projects.list_members(project.project_id)
    client.projects.add_member(project.project_id, "@bob", role="reviewer")

The member-management calls require the project owner role. A valid bearer token without the required project role receives a permission error; a caller with no visibility of the project receives a not-found response.

Calibration jobs and live versions follow the project#

A calibration job belongs to the prompt, skill or workflow it refines, so it is visible to exactly the callers who can see that target, and acting on it needs a project role:

ActionProject role needed
List or read a job, its targets, or its quality reviewsany member
Request changes on a candidate, or submit a quality reviewowner, editor or reviewer
Apply a candidate, promote a prompt version, or roll a prompt backowner or editor

A caller who is not a member of the project receives a not-found response, even when their token carries the global caliber.operator scope and even when the request names the project in X-CALIBER-Project. A member whose role is too weak receives a permission error. caliber.admin can read every project's jobs but, like every other role-gated action, is not an implicit member, so applying or rolling back needs a real role in that project.

Skills, tools, workflows and knowledge bases follow the project#

The same rule covers every other project-scoped family: a caller who is not a member of the project receives a not-found response, and a member whose role is too weak receives a permission error that names the role. What each role may do on a mutating route:

ActionProject role needed
Create or change a skill, tool, workflow, workflow version or knowledge base; clear workflow session memoryowner or editor
Publish a workflow version, promote or roll back an alias, publish or unpublish a workflow service, mint or revoke a service tokenowner or editor
Run a workflow or a tool, start a calibration, upload a file into a runowner, editor or reviewer
Record a test run or a baseline for a skill or tool; create or change a benchmark reportowner, editor or reviewer
Approve or reject a pending production promotion, or a run waiting for approvalowner or reviewer
Read, list, render, preview, validate, or queryany member

Creating a skill, tool, workflow or knowledge base is checked against the project named in X-CALIBER-Project. Registering, changing or archiving a tool, and changing or rolling back a skill, also need the global caliber.admin scope, which is checked first. Before this contract only the workflow, run and knowledge-base roots checked a project role, so a viewer could publish a workflow version, move a production alias, approve a pending production promotion, publish a workflow as a service and mint a bearer token for it, run a tool, replace its test cases, and queue a calibration. tests/test_extended_family_isolation.py sweeps every one of these routes as an outsider, a viewer, a reviewer and an editor.

What the alpha does not enforce#

  • Gate verdicts are not project-scoped. GET and POST /gate-verdicts/{artifact_type}/{version_key} key a verdict by a free-form string that names no artifact, so no project can be derived from it, and any operator can overwrite any verdict. The verdict is advisory: no Apply, promotion or release decision reads it, and the UI has no consumer for it.
  • Traces are not project-scoped. The observability pages and the trace and metric routes are open to every signed-in user, so anyone who can sign in can read traces and their payloads.
  • Apply has no second approver. An owner or editor reviews and applies in one step. The approval record created at Apply time is an audit and rollback anchor that names who applied.
  • CSRF protection is off by default. CALIBER_CSRF_ENABLED is false unless you set it, which assumes a loopback or trusted-network deployment. Enable it, with a signing secret, before exposing CALIBER more widely. See Alpha scope and limitations.

4. SDK path#

If you are writing Python, use the SDK unless you specifically need the raw wire layer.

Recommended path:

  1. SDK guide
  2. SDK API reference
  3. CLI and async client for operator-style automation

5. Raw HTTP path#

Use the REST API directly when:

  • you are integrating from another language
  • you need OpenAPI-driven tooling
  • you are debugging request/response behavior

Start from:

  1. REST API overview
  2. Authentication and conventions
  3. Resource catalog
  4. HTTP reference

6. Common failure modes#

SymptomFirst thing to check
Request is authenticated but sees the wrong objectsX-CALIBER-Project or SDK project scope
Project is visible but a write/publish is refusedaccess_role, permissions, and the token's global scope
Member routes return 403only the project owner can manage membership
Project route returns 404 unexpectedlythe caller is not an active member, owner, or admin
Write request fails in a browser-like flowmissing or stale CSRF token
HTTP integration works but Python code does notSDK client config, auth setup, or server compatibility
Python code works but raw HTTP does notmissing auth header, wrong base path, or missing project header
